answer: The meadow multiplier is published, charged in haven, and orchard lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2354 identities would post 2341 proofs and burn roughly 84 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
